abstract: The September 2026 edition of Revelio Labs' monthly AI Labor Market Tracker for the United States, released October 1, 2026 with most workforce data running through August 2026. The tracker reports five gauges - talent supply, labor demand, market equilibrium, work content and matching efficiency - built on Revelio's online professional profiles, job postings, salary records, employee reviews and WARN notices rather than payroll or survey data. This edition widens the early-career finding: employment for workers aged 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupations is down 20% relative to the least exposed since pre-ChatGPT, against 6% for older workers, up from 19% in Revelio's early-September read and 13% in the inaugural July edition. Several other gauges moved toward the less-alarming side of the ledger: the posting gap between most- and least-exposed occupations narrowed to -29% from -40% in July, the flow of new AI-adopting firms fell 17% versus July, and the share of workers with at least one reported AI skill slipped to 7.2% from 7.6%.
keyFindings: Employment for ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupations is down 20% relative to the least exposed since pre-ChatGPT, versus 6% for older workers
7.2% of US job positions were held by workers with at least one reported AI skill in August 2026, down from 7.6% in July
Gap in job postings between the most and least AI-exposed occupations narrowed to -29%, from -40% in July
New AI-adopting firms per month fell 17% compared with July; cumulative adoption reached roughly 7% of eligible hiring firms, up from 5.9% in the July edition
AI-adopting firms have grown headcount 27% more than non-adopters since November 2022, with senior roles +32% versus junior roles +6%
90% of year-over-year activity change occurs within occupations rather than through occupation-mix shifts, up from 89% in July
Recruiter-ghosting mentions are -1% versus the October 2022 baseline, reversing from +3% in July; job postings per external hire continued a six-year climb
Computer science and IT bachelor's degrees fell to 7.9% of degrees from a 2022 peak of 12.2%, while engineering rose to 17.8% from 10.9%
methodology: Event-study specifications with occupation and month fixed effects, following the design of Brynjolfsson, Chandar & Chen (2025), 'Canaries in the Coal Mine.' Exposure is assigned at the occupation level and contrasts are drawn between the most- and least-exposed groups. Firm AI adoption is identified from job postings - a firm is coded as adopting when it posts AI integrator roles. Work-content shifts are measured with an activity-mix dissimilarity index decomposed into within-occupation and between-occupation components. Matching efficiency uses employee-review text (recruiter ghosting, communication complaints) and postings-per-hire ratios.
qualifiers: Tier 2 - institutional analysis from a commercial labor data vendor, not peer-reviewed. Profile-based employment data skew toward white-collar and online-visible workers and carry reporting lags and self-report error, unlike payroll or survey universes. Headline figures are relative contrasts between exposure quintiles or between adopters and non-adopters, not economy-wide magnitudes, so they cannot be read as displacement shares. The adoption gauge (~7% of eligible hiring firms) is postings-derived and covers only firms that hire, a different instrument and population from the Census BTOS firm-adoption series. The talent-supply gauge counts AI skills reported on profiles, which is skill possession rather than observed AI use at work. The 20% early-career figure is a revision of the same measurement window as the 19% Revelio reported in early September, not an additional month of deterioration.
